docstring:
Schinzel conjectured (see [Si56]) the generalisation that, for any fixed $a$, if $n$ is sufficiently
large in terms of $a$ then there exist distinct integers $1\leq x < y < z$ such that
$\frac{a}{n} = \frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{1}{z}.$
references: [Si56](https://zbmath.org/?q=an%3A0075.03302) Sierpiński, W., Sur les décompositions de nombres rationnels en fractions primaires. Mathesis (1956), 16--32.
type_pretty: ∀ (a : ℕ), 0 < a → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ x y z, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < y ∧ y < z ∧ ↑a / ↑n = 1 / ↑x + 1 / ↑y + 1 / ↑z
